topic: The Triangle of Power: Unified Notation for Powers, Roots, and Logs
target_audience: High school students or introductory college mathematics students

sections.title: The Problem of Disjointed Symbols
lecture_lines: Traditional math notation can feel like separate languages.
We use different symbols for powers, roots, and logs.
Leo the Lion sees 2³, ∛8, and log₂(8).
These look different but describe the same relationship.
Let's find a way to unify these three ideas.
animations: Show the expressions 2^3=8, \u221b8=2, and log\u2082(8)=3 scattered in different colors (#FFD700, #1E90FF, #32CD32).
An icon labeled 'Leo' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lion.svg] (#FFFFFF) appears in the center, looking between the symbols with '?' marks.
Highlight the symbols ^, \u221a, and 'log' in bright red (#FF0000) to emphasize their differences.
Circle the numbers 2, 3, and 8 in all expressions with a single white circle (#FFFFFF).
Fade out the traditional symbols and move the numbers 2, 3, and 8 towards the center.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Three Roles
lecture_lines: Every exponential story has three essential parts.
The Base, the Exponent, and the Result.
Imagine a magic slime doubling over time.
animations: Display a 'Growth Machine' icon (#A9A9A9) with three empty slots.
Fill the first slot with a 'Base' slime [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/slime.svg] (#FFD700) and show a 'x2' multiplier.
Show a clock icon (#1E90FF) ticking 3 times to represent 'Exponent = 3'.

sections.title: The Solution: The Power Triangle
lecture_lines: Introducing the Triangle of Power for unified math.
Place the Base at the bottom-left corner.
Put the Exponent at the very top.
The Result sits at the bottom-right corner.
One geometric shape stores all three numbers perfectly.
animations: Draw a large equilateral triangle outline in white (#FFFFFF).
Place the text 'Base' and the number 2 at the bottom-left vertex (#FFD700).
Place the text 'Exponent' and the number 3 at the top vertex (#1E90FF).
Place the text 'Result' and the number 8 at the bottom-right vertex (#32CD32).
Flash the entire triangle once in gold (#FFD700) to signify unification.

sections.title: Operation 1: Solving for the Result (Powers)
lecture_lines: When we need the Result, we calculate powers.
Given a Base of 3 and Exponent of 2.
The missing bottom-right corner must be 9.
animations: Show the triangle [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/triangle.svg] with 3 at bottom-left and 2 at the top; bottom-right is a '?' (#FF4500).
Create a glowing yellow line (#FFFF00) connecting the Base (3) and Exponent (2).
The '?' at the bottom-right transforms into the number 9 in lime green (#32CD32).

sections.title: Operation 2: Solving for the Base (Roots)
lecture_lines: Solving for the Base replaces the radical symbol.
Root the Rabbit digs for the unknown bottom-left.
If Exponent is 3 and Result 64, Base is 4.
animations: Show the triangle with 3 at the top and 64 at bottom-right; bottom-left is '?' (#FF4500).
A small rabbit icon (#FFFFFF) appears and 'digs' at the bottom-left vertex.
The '?' at the bottom-left transforms into the number 4 in gold (#FFD700).

sections.title: Operation 3: Solving for the Exponent (Logarithms)
lecture_lines: Finding the Exponent replaces the "log" notation.
A rising balloon seeks the high top vertex.
With Base 5 and Result 25, Exponent is 2.
animations: Show the triangle with 5 at bottom-left and 25 at bottom-right; top is '?' (#FF4500).
A blue balloon icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/balloon.svg] (#1E90FF) floats from the bottom up to the top vertex.
The '?' at the top transforms into the number 2 in dodger blue (#1E90FF).

sections.title: Synthesis: The Beauty of Symmetry
lecture_lines: The triangle reveals hidden mathematical symmetry.
One static triangle covers all three operations.
Simply cover one corner to create a problem.
Powers, roots, and logs are now one story.
Math is simpler when we see the connections.
animations: Show the triangle with 2 (bottom-left), 10 (top), and 1024 (bottom-right).
A semi-transparent gray box (#A9A9A9) cycles through covering each corner one by one.
Highlight the 'Result' corner, then the 'Base' corner, then the 'Exponent' corner.
Remove the box and show all three numbers glowing in their respective colors.
The triangle scales up slightly and the traditional symbols (√, log) appear and then dissolve into the triangle.
